CitationAbsence.description:
Why a returned row carries no citation, typed rather than bare.

A sourceless row is NEVER omitted, because omitting it breaks the exhaustiveness guarantee that
is this read's whole product, and NEVER returned bare, because that recreates the missing-source
failure the work exists to fix. These are five different facts with five different repairs, so
collapsing them into "no source" would discard something a caller can act on.

**Five, and each is decided by something we hold rather than by the other four not applying.**
That matters to a reader of this list, because it is what makes the answer safe to act on: a
value here is never the runtime shrugging.

``source_undeclared``: the value WAS grounded in a passage and the evidence item carried nothing
to name it by. A gap in what the caller sent, and fixable by the caller: send a source reference
with the item. Note what decides it, because the naive reading is the opposite one: it is the
presence of a grounded passage with no name, not the absence of any record at all.

``ambiguous_match``: the value's wording was found in several evidence items, so no single source
can be attributed to it. Items sharing a long verbatim span are copies of one another rather than
independent witnesses, and attributing to one of them would silently turn one source into
several. ``matched_source_ids`` on the row names the items it was found in, so the answer is
"found in these, cannot attribute to one" rather than "no source".

``no_passage_lane``: the claim comes from a lane that has no passage to point at. A statement the
user made, free text inside a tool result, a structural field read from a keyed shape. Nothing is
missing and nothing is fixable, which is exactly why it is not reported as one of the two fixable
reasons above: told ``source_undeclared``, a caller would go looking for a reference to attach to
something that will never carry one.

``predates_citations``: the claim was recorded before this feature existed, so no passage was
captured for it. History rather than a defect, and no backfill can recover it: the spans that
grounded the value were never stored.

``citation_write_lost``: we DID have a passage for this claim and its citation record is not
there. A claim is committed in its own transaction and its citation follows in a second one that
is allowed to fail without losing the claim, so a table lock, an exhausted connection pool or a
policy refusal during a migration loses citations in bulk while every claim still lands. This is
a fault on our side, not a property of your corpus, and it is the one value here you should
raise with us rather than act on: the passage existed, and a repair on our side can recover the
reference. It is decided positively, from the marker the write path stamps when it HAS a
citation to write, never from the failure, which nothing at read time can observe.

Read the middle two together. Both mean nobody can do anything, and they say different things
about coverage: ``predates_citations`` is a statement about when the claim was written, and
``no_passage_lane`` is a statement about what kind of fact it is. Counting the second as the
first would report our coverage as historically limited when the truth is that the fact never
had a passage to cite.

And read ``citation_write_lost`` against ``no_passage_lane``, which is the conflation this fifth
value exists to end. Without it, every lost citation write arrived as ``no_passage_lane``, whose
published meaning is "nothing is missing and nothing is fixable" -- a deployment fault of ours
reported to a customer, in bulk, as a positive statement that these facts never had a source, on
the exact surface they check filenames on.

marked "no source declared" and a caller would read a deployment state as a fact about its
corpus.

``exhaustive`` means the lookup ran, so an empty ``citations`` on a row is that row's own answer
and its ``citation_absence`` says why. ``unavailable`` means it did not, so ``citations`` is

citation rather than two.

reference, which is every row today. The passage is deliberately not stored beside the claim: it
lives once, on the document that holds it, so erasing that document removes the quote everywhere

ClaimErasureReceipt.description:
The durable record of a claim-layer erasure.

``reached`` counts what the cascade actually removed from the claim layer; ``not_reached`` names
the stores this erasure deliberately does not touch (learnings, graph nodes, raw traces, usage
aggregates), so the receipt never overstates what was erased.

``reached`` also carries the withdrawal this erasure performed before deleting anything:
``mass_removed``, ``edges_repaired`` and ``learnings_touched``. Deleting rows proves storage
changed; only those three show that no rule still stands on evidence that no longer exists,
which is the part of an erasure a data-subject request actually asks about.

``reached`` also names what the erasure removed outside the claim tables, so a reader of the
receipt alone can see the whole reach: ``boundary_claim_offers`` and
``boundary_obligation_offers`` are the fact and obligation offer records purged from run state,
and ``obligations`` is the obligations deleted from the shelf itself.

``has_residue`` says the boundary purge did not reach every run holding this entity's offers.
``status`` alone cannot: it goes to ``complete`` when the sequence finishes, whether or not

ClaimWipeResponse.description:
What a whole-agent claim wipe erased.

Counts rather than receipts: a wipe writes one receipt per entity, and returning hundreds of
them inline would make the destructive call's response the largest in the API for no reader's
benefit. Every receipt is durable and listed by ``GET .../claims/erasures``, and
``request_ids`` names the ones this wipe wrote so a reader can go straight to them.

``has_residue`` is true when any of those receipts is, so an operator sees from the wipe alone
that some run still holds an erased entity's offers.

``remaining_entities`` is what makes the call repeatable rather than open-ended: one request
erases a bounded batch, and a non-zero count is the caller's instruction to come back. It counts
the corpus after the pass, so a run that harvested a fact mid-wipe shows up here rather than
being quietly missed.

``attributes_removed`` is only ever non-zero on the pass that empties the corpus, since the
vocabulary is shared and cannot go while an entity still needs it. It reports zero if that sweep
itself failed, which understates the reach rather than overstating it.

different meaning, as the consent ETag on claim review; one header with two unrelated meanings

Request to create a space.

The kind is fixed to ``domain`` server-side; the name and an optional external
registration are caller-supplied. ``registration`` is the one genuinely optional
field on this surface, and legitimately so: omitting it and sending it as null both
mean "created unregistered", so nothing here turns on telling absent from null.

``extra="forbid"`` matches its sibling, and earns its place at exactly this change: a
client still sending the superseded flat ``external_system``/``external_id`` would
otherwise have them silently dropped and get back a space created with no registration
at all, which is the failure mode hardest to notice and slowest to diagnose.

Why a turn ended with nothing worth learning.

A closed set: an unrecognised value is rejected rather than stored, so the
column stays queryable and cannot accrue junk cardinality. These mirror the
gates a host applies before shipping an episode, and they are what makes an
otherwise invisible client-side decision measurable.

DeclineRequest.description:
Close a run whose turn ended with nothing worth learning.

The terminal counterpart to observe/reinforce. A host that resolves and then
finds the turn not worth learning from must say so rather than going silent:
silence is indistinguishable from a host that broke, and that ambiguity is
what makes a loop-closure alert uninterpretable.

Declining does not add the episode to the corpus. It records the run as
closed, attributes it to a host, and settles the resolve reservation.

agent_name.description: Human-readable agent name, unique within your tenant. This is not the hosted agent UUID used in `/agents/{agent_id}` REST paths. If no agent with this name exists yet, a write-scoped call (`agents:write`) creates a minimal learning agent in your tenant. `POST /resolve` with only `agents:read` looks up an existing name and does not insert. Reuse the same name on resolve, observe, reinforce, and distill to target the same learning corpus. Clients conventionally namespace an agent-loop `run_id` as `<agent_name>:...`; if yours does, avoid the name `distill`, because `distill:` is reserved for corpus distillation run ids and every agent-loop write would be refused.
agent_name.title: Agent Name

is_delivered.description: Whether this turn's recall was delivered in a way the turn can be credited for. A turn can receive the injection and still decline, so this decides whether the resolve is billed or released: the caller is charged for the resolve this turn consumed, never for one it did not. A warm stash reports false and is not charged even though the model saw it, because the block was resolved on an earlier turn and this turn consumed no resolve of its own. Whether that earlier turn was itself charged is that turn's own report, not something this field asserts. Omitted means the host did not report either way, which is recorded as unknown rather than as a definite non-delivery: the credit alert separates a decline that lost credit from one that never had any to lose, and a default of false would silently file every omitting client under the second.
is_delivered.title: Is Delivered

obligation_outcomes.description: Obligations this turn resolved. Present on decline as well as on reinforce because the two questions are independent: a turn can produce nothing worth learning and still have closed something the shelf was owed, and a host forced to choose would either lose the closure or credit an episode it had already judged not worth crediting. Ids the run never offered are counted and dropped, never refused.
obligation_outcomes.title: Obligation Outcomes

reason.description: Why the turn had nothing worth learning from.

recall_outcome.description: Why the recall earned nothing this turn, from the same closed set reinforce uses. A declined turn that was never shown its learnings is a different run from one that was shown them and did too little to be worth learning from, and different again from one shown a warm stash it can never be credited for. Sending this without `is_delivered` is enough: the flag is derived from it. Sending both with different meanings is not refused, it is reconciled in favour of this field and the disagreement is logged.

run_id.description: The caller-owned `run_id` supplied to resolve; it must not start with `distill:`, which is reserved for distillation jobs.
run_id.title: Run Id

source_framework.description: Producing host/framework, used to attribute the per-host funnel. Optional; the server derives one when it is absent. `unknown` is reserved: the loop-closure funnel groups runs with no attribution under that label and excludes them from alerting, so a value equal to it is normalised to unset rather than stored as a host.
source_framework.title: Source Framework

DeterministicArmReport.description:
What the exhaustive arm delivered, including the case where it failed to be exhaustive.

``total`` is a true count over every entity the name probe reached, taken from the claim shelf
itself rather than from the bounded snapshot the recall path materialises. That distinction is
the reason this surface exists: a count taken off the snapshot cannot see the rows the snapshot
already dropped, which on a real corpus is most of them.

``guarantee`` downgrades to ``partial`` with a stated ``downgrade_reason`` when the read's own
statement ceiling fires or the name probe hits its match bound, and ``is_total_exact`` goes false
with it. That pair is what stops a truncated set reading as a complete one.

downgrade_reason.description: Why the guarantee is `partial`, in plain words. Null when it is `exhaustive`.
downgrade_reason.title: Downgrade Reason

entities_reached.description: How many entities the question's names reached. Zero is a real answer, not a failure.
entities_reached.title: Entities Reached

held_count.description:
Rows held back pending human review, counted and never returned. Counted rather than silently dropped so a caller can tell a held row from an absent one; not returned because content no human has released is not something a caller can be told to trust.

**Null means the count did not run**, which is a different fact from zero and is why it is nullable rather than defaulted. The count shares the deterministic arm's statement ceiling, so when that ceiling fires there is no measurement to report, and reporting an unmeasured zero would commit the exact error this field exists to prevent: a held row reading as an absent one. `is_total_exact` says the same thing about `total`; this says it about the count, with no room for a flag to disagree. Expect null on precisely the responses where `guarantee` is `partial`.
held_count.title: Held Count

is_total_exact.description: Whether `total` is a count or a floor. Check it before quoting the number.
is_total_exact.title: Is Total Exact

scoped_entity_ids.description: The entities this answer was narrowed to: the ones the question named that documents are filed under. Empty when the answer was not narrowed.
scoped_entity_ids.title: Scoped Entity Ids

total.description: How many claims this arm's scope holds. Exact when `is_total_exact`, otherwise a lower bound: never fewer than the rows already returned, because claiming less than we handed over would be false.
total.title: Total

withheld_by_scope.description:
Rows this agent holds that the question's own containers do not reach, counted and never returned. A claim is withheld when its document belongs only to OTHER containers and the claim is not itself about one you bound: one engagement's facts arriving inside another's answer is the leak this closes.

**Counted rather than silently dropped**, for the reason `held_count` is: a reader who cannot tell a withheld row from an absent one cannot tell "we do not hold that" from "we are not showing you that". Zero means nothing was withheld, which includes every read that was not narrowed. **Null when the narrowing or its count did not complete**, and `downgrade_reason` says which: an unresolved scope leaves the answer unnarrowed with `total` measured, an incomplete count leaves it narrowed with `total` a lower bound.

When measured, `total` already excludes these, so `total` and the rows you can page to agree; this number says how many the narrowing removed.
withheld_by_scope.title: Withheld By Scope

DeterministicArmReport.title: DeterministicArmReport

DocumentCitationRequest.description:
The span of a stored document this evidence was drawn from.

**All six members or none, and that is enforced by them being required here rather than
checked later.** Core's `citation_pointer` returns a pointer only when all six survived
admission, because five of six is a span with no end, or an end with no document, and
resolving one would mean inventing the missing member. A model where each was optional would
let a caller send five, have it silently ignored, and be told nothing.

`doc_id` is bounded in BYTES, from the store's own bound, and is NOT stripped. Both are the
store's rules rather than choices made here: the key is the caller's identity for the
document, so trimming it would silently make two of their documents one, and a character bound
against a byte store lets a multibyte key mint a pointer to a document that can never exist.

The other five rules the store enforces on a document key (no `..`, no leading separator, no
empty segment, no backslash, no control character) are NOT re-derived here. A check that
duplicates another component's rule and gets a fraction of it is worse than no check, because
it reads as one; the service layer calls the store's own `validate_doc_id` on the way through.

Restated beside the other four question-read vocabularies, and for their reason: it is a closed
set the runtime decides, so publishing it as a bare string documents no values, gives a client
nothing to branch on, and lets a runtime rename reach a caller with nothing to catch it.
``claims_question_parity_test`` compares this against the runtime's own enum once the pin ships
it, which is the point of restating rather than inventing.

An alias match is not a weaker match, it is a less direct one: aliases are harvested from the
sources themselves, which is why a meeting that mentions an account in passing is reachable at
all, and also why a generic recorded alias can reach very widely. The two are kept apart
everywhere they appear precisely so that width stays attributable.

one of the three that was written and never read, because the ladder admits a form onto the
surface registry rather than onto the alias table, so a form graded active bound on the goal
path and was invisible to a question. Same interlock as `QuestionReadArm.CONCERNS`: this copy
is constructed strictly from Core's value at `claims_question_read_service.py:437` and `:509`,

declared_sensitivity.description: Optional caller-declared metadata for this item, in the same vocabulary as a step's. Nest these members under a `provenance` key, e.g. `{"provenance": {"source_id": "...", "channel": "..."}}`; a flat top-level `source_id` (or `channel`, `genre`, `author`, `source_time`, `source_class`) is refused rather than silently read as no declaration. The record may also carry a citation into a stored document: `doc_id`, `text_sha256` and `segmenter_version` as strings, and `unit_index`, `start` and `end` as INTEGERS, naming the exact passage this item's evidence was drawn from. A numeric string for an offset is refused deliberately, because it is a second shape for the same pointer. `attacker_reachable` is a BOOLEAN: `true` says someone outside your organisation can write into this source, and holds what is read from it as untrusted. `false` is ignored, because a source vouching for itself is not believed. The `provenance` record says where the item came from, in two independent facets plus identity: `channel` is how it reached you (chat, email, meeting, document_store, system_of_record, api) and conditions how fast it goes stale; `genre` is what kind of artefact it is (policy, plan, minutes, reference, correspondence, note, aside) and conditions how authoritative it is. A signed policy pasted into a chat thread is both, which is why they are separate. Also `source_id`, `author`, and an RFC 3339 `source_time` for when the facts in it became true. An unrecognised `channel` or `genre` is kept verbatim and left unranked rather than refused. `source_class` is the superseded single-facet form, still accepted and never ranked. To say what the item is *about*, use the `subject` field above rather than this record.

identity_markers.description: Optional caller hints for people in this item: fuller names, emails, or Slack ids. Must appear verbatim in content or they are dropped. Distill also harvests those forms automatically when they sit next to the name.

obligations.description: Typed obligations this item already carries, written verbatim with no LLM involved: they are stored directly on the obligation shelf as provenance_class=user_directed and never enter this item's extraction. A relative due phrase ('next Friday') is refused at request validation rather than resolved; pre-resolve it before sending. Up to 8 per item, 50 across a request. Each obligation's own outcome (written, deduped, or a refusal) is reported on GET /learning-runs/{run_id}/status, not on the 202 this request returns.

record_context.description:
What your connector knows about the document this item came from: which accounts it belongs to, who was on it, and what it answers. A declaration, and the only rung that can reach a document whose text names no account.

Sent as its own typed field rather than inside `declared_sensitivity`, so the shapes are in this schema and a malformed one is a 422 naming the field rather than a value accepted and dropped later. A `record_context` key inside `declared_sensitivity` is ignored, for the same reason `subject` is: one concept, one way to declare it.

It is checked by the runtime's own rules at this door, and it needs a `source_ref` or an identifier to be filed under; one with neither is refused.

source_ref.description: Non-secret provenance: a doc id or URL. This is the input that decides whether a claim distilled from this item can name where it came from. A claim grounded in a passage of this item carries this string back as its citation's `grounding_ref`, so a later question read answers with the filename you sent. Omit it and the claim is still recorded and still returned, but with `citation_absence: source_undeclared` instead of a citation, and the name cannot be recovered afterwards because it was never sent. Send it whenever the item has a source, even a rough one.
source_ref.title: Source Ref

subject.description: The entity this item is about, e.g. an account or product name. Given, it is the name **every** fact from this item is filed under: it outranks the entity extraction reads out of the prose, so a fact about a person named inside the item is filed under this subject too. That is what stops one entity fragmenting across two spellings and never accumulating corroboration, and it is why the field suits an item your connector already knows is about exactly one thing, such as an account note matched to a CRM record. Omit it for an item covering several entities, a meeting transcript most of all, and each fact resolves its own entity from the prose. Sending the item's title here files the whole meeting under the meeting. To say where an item came from rather than what it is about, use `source_ref` or the provenance record.

ObligationClosureResult.description:
What became of one reported outcome, so a host can tell a recorded close from a discarded one.

A batch of outcomes can partly apply, and until this existed every mix of applied, ignored and
unknown ids came back as the same 202. This is the per-item result partly applying batch writes
settled on long ago (Elasticsearch's bulk API, BigQuery insertAll, HTTP 207): the request is
still accepted, and each id says for itself what happened to it.

"busy" is the only transient disposition and the only one worth sending again: the outcome was
neither applied nor judged. Reinforce does not produce it, since a close takes no run lock;
it stays in the vocabulary for callers written against it. "refused" is terminal, and
the two are deliberately different words, because a caller that retries a refusal loops for
ever and one that abandons a busy close loses it.

disposition.description: applied: the row moved to the requested terminal state. already_closed: it was already in exactly that state, so nothing moved and nothing is wrong. conflicting_close: a different terminal state holds, and the report was dropped rather than allowed to overwrite it. not_offered: this run was never shown that id, which is the disposition a stale id carried across turns gets. not_found: the id was offered and the row is no longer on the shelf. refused: the shelf rejected the write, from a version race or a note it would not take; terminal, do not resend. busy: this was not attempted; transient, and the same outcome may be sent again. Not produced by reinforce, whose closes take no run lock.
disposition.title: Disposition

id.description: The obligation id the reported outcome named.
id.title: Id

status.description: The row's status after the call, when the row exists. Null for not_offered, not_found and busy, where there is no row this call read.
status.title: Status

ObligationOpenCountResponse.description:
The metered open-obligation stock beside the live one, so a drift is visible rather than assumed.

``obligation_open_count`` is a stock counter: a nightly reconcile snapshots how many open
obligations a tenant holds. Every other obligation counter is flow, drained from events, and a
flow counter that stops being written is obviously wrong. A stock counter that stops being
written is not: it goes on reading as whatever it last said, which is exactly what a reader
would expect a healthy counter to look like on a quiet day. So the metered figure is only
meaningful next to the live one.

is_reconciled.description: True when the two agree and false when the metered figure has drifted. Null when there is nothing to reconcile against: either the reconcile has not written for this day (metered_reconciled_at is null) or the caller is space-filtered and there is no tenant-wide live figure. An unwritten day is deliberately not reported as drift, because for most of every day that is the healthy state.
is_reconciled.title: Is Reconciled

is_space_filtered.description: True when the caller's readable spaces are a subset of the tenant's, so live_open_count covers only those spaces. The metered figure is tenant-wide and is withheld in that case, because the reconciliation it exists for is a tenant-level question and comparing a space-narrowed live count against a tenant-wide meter reports drift that is only the caller's own visibility.
is_space_filtered.title: Is Space Filtered

live_open_count.description: Open obligations counted now. Across the tenant's agents for a caller with org-wide space access, and across the caller's readable spaces otherwise; is_space_filtered says which, and the two are not comparable.
live_open_count.title: Live Open Count

metered_open_count.description: usage_daily.obligation_open_count for that day, or null when the reconcile has not written for it yet. Null is not zero: an unwritten day and a tenant with no open obligations are different facts.
metered_open_count.title: Metered Open Count

metered_reconciled_at.description: When the stock reconcile last wrote for this tenant-day, or null when it never has. This, and not the count, is what says whether the metered figure is a measurement: obligation_open_count is not-null with a default of 0, so a tenant that merely made a request that day carries a zero nothing measured.
metered_reconciled_at.title: Metered Reconciled At

usage_date.description: The metered day, in UTC, the stock figure was read for.

QuestionClaimReadRequest.description:
One page of a question-shaped read.

``as_of`` is captured on the first page and handed back; return it with every later page and the
whole walk is a stable snapshot rather than a moving target under the corroboration and
supersession writes happening underneath it. It costs one predicate and materialises nothing.
Omit it on the first page; it is not a filter to set by hand, and setting it forward buys nothing
while setting it back hides the agent's recent facts from the caller's own read.

**Unknown fields are rejected.** Two of the five fields here are what make the walk honest, and
both are the kind a caller mistypes: ``as_of`` pins the snapshot, ``cursor`` makes the walk a
walk. Discarded silently, a misspelled ``asOf`` returns a 200 read against a fresh snapshot to a
caller who believes they pinned one, and a misspelled ``cursor`` returns page one for ever to a
caller who believes they are walking. That is the exact silent-success shape this whole surface
exists to remove, so it cannot be the shape of its own request handling.

examples.question: What did we agree with Harlow Freight about the two-column layout?

as_of.description: The snapshot this page reads against, as an instant. Omit on the first page and send back the `as_of` the response returned on every page after it. A value with no offset is read as UTC, which is also what comes back, so the walk is never pinned to a different instant than the one you meant.
as_of.title: As Of

cursor.description: An opaque cursor from a previous page's `next_cursor`. Null for the first page. It encodes a position rather than an offset, so a page is neither skipped nor repeated when rows are written underneath the walk.
cursor.title: Cursor

include_superseded.description: Include values that were replaced, in order along the chain, for a history question. Off by default because a superseded value WAS replaced and returning it as current is a lie. Note this is a different thing from a stale value, which nothing replaced and which is returned by default carrying `is_stale`.
include_superseded.title: Include Superseded

page_size.description: Rows per page. This bounds a page, never the answer: the deterministic arm is exhaustive and keyset-paged, so nothing is hidden past this number and it decides only how many round trips reading everything takes.
page_size.title: Page Size

question.description: The question to answer from this agent's claims. Names in it are matched against the entities the agent has recorded, exactly and after normalisation only: there is no fuzzy matching here, and approximate matching is the recall arm's job and is labelled as such. A question naming no recorded entity is a valid call that returns the recall arm alone.
examples: What did we agree with Harlow Freight about the two-column layout?
question.title: Question

QuestionClaimReadRequest.title: QuestionClaimReadRequest

QuestionClaimReadResponse.description:
One page of claims for a question, with each arm's guarantee stated beside it.

Two arms and two guarantees, never one blended list with an exactness flag. The blended
alternative is simpler to consume and gives up the coverage statement that is the whole value:
read `deterministic.guarantee` and `deterministic.total` first, because they are what answers
"is this everything you hold", and read `recall` as a set of suggestions that answer nothing of
the kind.

as_of.description: The snapshot this page was read against. Send it back with the cursor on every later page; a walk that does not is reading a moving target.
as_of.title: As Of

next_cursor.description: The position to resume from, or null when the deterministic arm has no more rows. Null is a statement that the walk is finished, not an invitation to try again: a cursor is never issued for a page that would return nothing.
next_cursor.title: Next Cursor

ordering.description: Which ordering THIS page carries. It changes between the first page and the rest.

reach.description: How far each of the question's matched surfaces reached, one row per surface and match kind, so an over-broad match is visible in the response rather than only inferable from the rows. Read `entities_reached` for the magnitude, which is exact, and `entity_ids` for as much of the inventory as fits.
reach.title: Reach

QuestionClaimReadResponse.title: QuestionClaimReadResponse

QuestionClaimRow.description:
One claim as this read returns it: the whole value, its trust axes, and how it was reached.

The value is WHOLE. The per-claim character bound that exists elsewhere governs what the platform
renders into a prompt under a token budget; it was never a statement about what a caller may know
about its own agent's shelf, and a prefix here would be an answer that silently omits its own
tail.

Plain text rather than the defanged ``RenderedText`` the curation models carry, and the
difference is deliberate. Curation shows attacker-reachable prose to a HUMAN in a console, where
a defanged URL is a safety feature. This is a data read whose consumer renders the fact itself:
a value with its URLs rewritten is a different value, and a filename with its dots escaped fails
the very check this surface exists to pass. The caller is the party deciding how to display it,
which is also why the trust axes below travel with every row instead of being collapsed into a
score.

arms.description: Which arms returned this row. A row carrying only `recall` is a suggestion, not part of any completeness statement.
arms.title: Arms

attribute_key.description: The slot this value was filed under, or null when it was recorded without one. A null is not a defect: a value nothing could be filed under is still held, and is still returned here, because withholding it would be the omission this read exists to remove.
attribute_key.title: Attribute Key

channel_trust.description: How much authority the channel the value arrived on earns on its own.
channel_trust.title: Channel Trust

citation_absence.description:
Why `citations` is empty, present only when it is AND only when the citation lookup actually ran. Read the response-level `citations.guarantee` first: when that is `unavailable` this field is deliberately null on every row, because there is nothing to explain about a claim we did not look up.

Two of the four values name work you can do (`source_undeclared`, `ambiguous_match`) and two name work nobody can do (`no_passage_lane`, `predates_citations`). Branch on that split rather than on emptiness, which cannot tell them apart.

citations.description: Where this value was read from, zero or more. Plural because a value corroborated across three meetings has three passages, and 'which meetings does this come from' is a question a single source field cannot answer.
citations.title: Citations

contradicts.description: The claims this row contradicts, empty where none. BOTH sides of an unresolved contradiction are always returned and each names the other; returning one side is a silently resolved conflict, and that is a defect rather than a mode a caller may choose. This is not a flag: there is no request field that turns it off.
contradicts.title: Contradicts

document_occurred_at.description: That document's declared date. Null when it declared none; an ingest time is never shown as a meeting date.
document_occurred_at.title: Document Occurred At

document_ref.description: The document this claim was read from, or null when it names none.
document_ref.title: Document Ref

entity_name.description: The entity this claim is about, so a row can be read without a second lookup.
entity_name.title: Entity Name

is_caller_declared.description: True when the provenance on this row is what the caller said it was rather than something the platform observed. Published because a caller weighing its own facts should know which of them it vouched for itself.
is_caller_declared.title: Is Caller Declared

is_contradiction_partner.description: True when this row was pulled onto this page to complete a contradiction pair rather than reached by the page's own ordering. Such a row may appear again on the page its own position belongs to; that duplication is deliberate, and the alternative is not returning it at all.
is_contradiction_partner.title: Is Contradiction Partner

is_document_date_declared.description: Whether the document declared its date. Null when there is no document or its record could not be read.
is_document_date_declared.title: Is Document Date Declared

is_operator_asserted.description: True when a human operator asserted this value rather than it being extracted.
is_operator_asserted.title: Is Operator Asserted

is_stale.description: True when the value has decayed on the currency axis: nothing has replaced it, so it IS the current value, and it is merely old. This is a different fact from being superseded, and conflating the two causes the failure that withholding both looks like it prevents: a decayed value withheld is an omission, a superseded value returned as current is a lie. Decayed values are returned, marked; superseded ones are not.
is_stale.title: Is Stale

is_tainted.description: True when the value reached us through content that could have been authored to influence us.
is_tainted.title: Is Tainted

last_observed_at.description: The most recent time a source restated this value. Read it beside recorded_at: a value recorded once in March and restated last week is a different thing from one nobody has mentioned since.
last_observed_at.title: Last Observed At

matched_source_ids.description: Present only with an `ambiguous_match` absence: the evidence items the value was found in. 'Found in these, cannot attribute to one' is strictly more than silence.
matched_source_ids.title: Matched Source Ids

matched_via.description: Every route that reached this row's entity. Empty when the row arrived through the recall arm alone, which is itself the useful signal: nothing in the question named this entity, an approximate search found it.
matched_via.title: Matched Via

passage.description: The passage of the stored document this claim was read from, resolved at read time.
passage.title: Passage

passage_absence.description: Why `passage` is null, typed rather than bare.

provenance.description: Where this value came from, as declared and as resolved: the channel, the genre, the source identifier and the author the caller stated, beside the closed vocabularies those resolved to. Both halves, because a caller weighing its own facts needs to see that a source called itself a policy AND whether that word was recognised; a resolved value alone hides an unrecognised declaration behind 'unknown', and a declared value alone cannot say whether anything ranks on it. The same record every other claim surface publishes, off the same column.

provenance_class.description: How far the source was from the agent: its own output, a tool, or a third party.
provenance_class.title: Provenance Class

recorded_at.description: When this version of the value was written. Half of the paging key.
recorded_at.title: Recorded At

statement.description: The claim as a standalone sentence, whole and uncut.
statement.title: Statement

status.description: Where this row sits in its own history: open, or disputed by an alternative that has not been settled. Superseded rows are excluded unless include_superseded was set.
status.title: Status

superseded_by_claim_id.description: On a superseded row, the claim that replaced it.
superseded_by_claim_id.title: Superseded By Claim Id

supersedes_id.description: The claim this one replaced, or the incumbent it is disputing. It is the link the supersession chain is walked along, and with include_superseded it is how a history question is answered.
supersedes_id.title: Supersedes Id

valid_from.description: When the value started being true in the world, which is not when it was recorded.
valid_from.title: Valid From

valid_until.description: When the value stopped being true, where that is known. Null means still in force.
valid_until.title: Valid Until

value_num.description: The value as a number, when it is one.
value_num.title: Value Num

value_text.description: The value itself, separated from the sentence around it so it can be compared.
value_text.title: Value Text

value_time.description: The value as a time, when it is one.
value_time.title: Value Time

value_type.description: How to read the value: text, a number, a time, and so on.
value_type.title: Value Type

withheld_contradiction_count.description:
How many of this row's contradiction partners exist but are held rather than returned. Zero on almost every row, and load-bearing where it is not.

The both-sides promise on `contradicts` has exactly one lawful exception: a hold keeps back content no human has released, so a held partner is not returned. Without this number an incumbent whose every dissenter is held comes back with an empty `contradicts` and is indistinguishable from a claim nothing disputes, which is the silently resolved conflict the promise exists to refuse, arriving through the one door the completion pass does not watch.

So read it as: this answer has a disputed side you are not being shown. Non-zero here with an empty `contradicts` means the only dissent on this value is held, and the value should not be quoted as uncontested. The agent-wide `held_count` cannot do this job, because it cannot be attributed to a row and so cannot tell you WHICH of your answers is missing a half.
withheld_contradiction_count.title: Withheld Contradiction Count

QuestionClaimRow.title: QuestionClaimRow

QuestionReadArm.description:
Which arm reached a row, because the two arms make different promises about it.

Carried per row rather than only per arm, because a row can be reached by both and because a row
reached ONLY by recall is a different fact for the reader: nothing about it was enumerated, so it
is a suggestion where a row from the deterministic arm is an answer.

CONCERNS is the third, and it is an arm rather than a label because it makes the deterministic
arm's kind of promise: exhaustive over its scope, keyset-paged and counted. A row carrying only
that stamp is a claim stated IN one of the account's documents rather than ABOUT the account.

THE MEMBER IS HERE BECAUSE THE PIN CANNOT MOVE WITHOUT IT. This enum is constructed strictly
from Core's value in `claims_question_read_service.py`, with no `_missing_` hook, so a Core that
can send `concerns` against a copy that cannot name it raises `ValueError` on the route rather
than degrading. That made a two-member copy the interlock in front of four merged Core pull
requests, which is section 213 of `platform-followups.md`.
QuestionReadArm.title: QuestionReadArm

QuestionSurfaceReach.description:
One matched surface, how it matched, and how far it reached. The fan-out disclosure.

What the response says about the question's own breadth, so an over-broad match is visible
before a single row is read rather than only inferable from the rows afterwards. The name probe
deliberately returns EVERY entity carrying a matched surface instead of one winner, which is what
makes it possible to answer "everything we hold about this account" across four separate meeting
records; the cost is that one very generic recorded alias can reach thousands of entities, and
this is where a caller sees that happening.

**The count is exact and is never cut. Only the id list is bounded.** That split is the whole
design. A surface that reached four thousand entities says four thousand here whether or not a
single id survives the cap, so the magnitude of a fan-out is always complete; bounding the count
as well would let a wide match read as a narrow one, which is exactly the narrowing this read
exists to refuse.

**Rows are keyed on (surface, how it matched), not on the surface alone.** The same word can be
one entity's registered name and another's recorded alias, and those are different findings: an
alias reaching four thousand records says something about how aliases are harvested, a name
reaching them says something else entirely. One row per pairing keeps them apart.

entities_reached.description: How many distinct entities this surface reached, exactly. Never truncated, whatever `entity_ids` holds: this is the number to read when judging whether a question matched too broadly.
entities_reached.title: Entities Reached

entity_ids.description:
Which entities, up to 500 per surface, in the order the agent's own registry returns them, so the sample is deterministic rather than arbitrary. When `len(entity_ids) < entities_reached` the list is the head of a longer set: there is no separate flag to read, because a flag beside the two numbers is a third thing that can disagree with them.

Two things this deliberately does not give you, rather than leave you to find out. Entity NAMES do not travel here, so naming an entity that has no row on the page you are holding takes a follow-up read; every returned row still carries its own entity name and its own `matched_via`. And past 500 entities on one surface this is a sample while `entities_reached` stays exact, so you always have the full magnitude and not always the full inventory.
entity_ids.title: Entity Ids

matched_as.description: Whether this surface matched entities by their own name or by an alias recorded for them. A surface that did both appears twice, once per kind, because the two say different things about why the match was as wide as it was.

surface.description: The text from the question that matched something the agent has recorded.
surface.title: Surface

QuestionSurfaceReach.title: QuestionSurfaceReach

held_unit_indices.description: Each unit of this note a dispute or identity hold covers, with the version it indexes. Findings citing one of them carry `rests_on_held`.

is_claims_on_earlier_version.description: True when the note's text was read at its current version but some of its claims were read from an earlier one, so a passage may differ from the text around it.

ReadGuarantee.description:
What an arm claims about its own completeness. This is the read's actual product.

``exhaustive`` means the arm enumerated everything in its scope and the total beside it is exact.
That is the statement a caller can check against an answer key ("is this everything you hold
about this account"), and it is the only one of these that can be checked.

``partial`` means an arm that promises exhaustive did not finish: the database's own statement
ceiling fired, or the name probe hit its match bound. It exists so a truncated set is never
returned still labelled exhaustive.

``best_effort`` is the recall arm's normal state: bounded, approximate, and ordered by an index
whose scan is not stable across two calls.

``unavailable`` is an arm that did not run. The call still succeeds, because the arm carrying the
guarantee never depends on the arm that does not.

Reporting a total's status rather than a bare number follows the tracked-total relation search
engines use: a count says whether it is exact or a lower bound rather than leaving a consumer to

RecallOutcome.description:
What became of a run's recall, as the client that owns the loop observed it.

A run that credits nothing has one signature at this boundary, an absent receipt,
and three causes that license different responses. The recall never reached the
model, in which case there is nothing to vouch for and the client is correct. It was
shown and the record of it could not be read back, which is a wiring defect. Or what
the model saw was a warm stash carried over from an earlier turn of the same project,
which was genuinely shown and can never be credited, because it was resolved against
a different goal and carries no run marker for a receipt to match. The receipt alone
cannot tell the three apart, so the client says which.

A closed set, like ``DeclineReason``: an unrecognised value is rejected rather than
stored, so the column stays queryable and cannot accrue junk cardinality. It is the
same set the client declares in ``hyperstruck/ide/recall.py``, and a member the
client can send and this one cannot costs that run its whole episode rather than
merely its diagnostic, because the request model forbids an unknown value. A new
member lands here first.

ResolveFactLane.description:
Why the fact lane returned what it returned, so an empty one can be read correctly.

An empty ``offered_claim_ids`` has always had several causes that call for opposite actions,
and until this existed they were indistinguishable in the response. The agent genuinely holds
nothing about the entities in this goal; the goal named no entity it has ever recorded; the
lane was switched off for this request; the lane was never wired; or the lane ran and gave up.
The first two are facts about the corpus and need nothing done. The last three are facts about
the deployment, and the last one is a defect.

This is not hypothetical, and the field exists because of a specific incident. A wall-clock
budget on the claim bind expired on every hosted resolve, so ``/resolve`` answered 200 with an
empty claim list and a null fact block on an agent holding thirteen open claims, one of them on
the entity named in the goal. That reads exactly like an agent with nothing to say. A customer
evaluating the product reasonably wrote it up as claim retrieval not working, and the failure
ran for days because nothing in the response could contradict that reading.

``is_complete`` is the field a measurement should key on, and it asks a different question from
``is_degraded``. A bind cut short by a cap ran successfully and returned real facts, so it is
not degraded, and it is still the wrong denominator: a rule whose evidence sat in an abandoned
dossier would be scored as ungrounded, and a deployment problem would be recorded as a fact
about the corpus.

is_degraded.description: Whether the lane failed to run, as opposed to running and finding nothing. True is an operational problem on our side, not a fact about the caller's corpus.

ResolveResponse.description:
What this run was offered: three separately placeable blocks and the ids behind them.

``injected_text`` carries the advice half (rules, plus the annotations compiled from
proceduralised learnings). ``injected_facts_text`` carries the fenced block of facts the agent
established about entities it has already investigated, on its own so a host can place it where
its model treats it best and keep the more stable advice half in a cached prompt prefix.
Separation costs attribution nothing: a receipt is the prompt as sent, and each half is matched
within it rather than by position.

``offered_claim_ids`` mirrors the fact block in first-emission order and is render-confirmed: a
fact refused by the trust floor or cut by the lane's token budget appears in neither.

``injected_obligations_text`` is the third block: the small set of open obligations that bear on
this moment, by their dates, by an entity this goal bound, or because what one rested on has
changed. It is advisory and each of its lines says so. An agent owing nothing due gets ``None``
rather than an empty block, which is why a host must place it conditionally.

``offered_obligation_ids`` is deliberately *not* render-confirmed the way ``offered_claim_ids``
is: it names everything the selection admitted, including an obligation the block's token
budget then cut. Offered and delivered are two records because the shelf escalates on
deliveries, and an obligation no model was shown must not be escalated for being ignored.

``fact_lane`` says why the fact block is what it is. This server always sends it, including when
the lane produced facts, because a caller that only receives it on failure has to know to look
for it, and the whole point is that the failure looked like success. It is nonetheless typed as
optional, and that is not hedging: a client deserialising a response from a deployment older
than this change must not fail on its absence, and treating "the field is missing" as "the lane
is fine" is the reading this whole field exists to stop. Absent means unknown.

claims.description: The recalled facts as data rather than as our prose, for a host that renders them under its own design. Carries every fact this agent's own planner would read, each with the trust axes and provenance the rendering decision needs, including the facts from attacker-reachable channels that an operator has released, which `injected_facts_text` cannot show. Null when the fact lane is unavailable or the recall bound no entity; never an empty entity list.

delivered_obligation_ids.description: The subset of `offered_obligation_ids` the block actually carried, after the token budget. Offered and delivered are two records for this shelf and only this shelf, because it escalates on deliveries: an obligation no model was shown must not be escalated for being ignored. A host holding only the offered set cannot tell one from the other, and neither can a client library building an episode from this response. Empty when the block carried nothing, which is not the same as offering nothing.
delivered_obligation_ids.title: Delivered Obligation Ids

fact_lane.description: Why the fact lane returned what it returned. Present on every resolve. Read it before concluding from an empty `offered_claim_ids` that the agent holds no facts: only outcome 'no_match' means that.

learnings.description: The offered learnings' evidence as data, mirroring the `Source:` line in `injected_text` without our prose. Null when no learning was offered; never an empty list.

The rendered block beside this carries our own wording, and the floor that governs it is about
what we may put into a prompt we did not author. It was never a statement about what a caller
may know about its own agent's shelf, which the claims API already serves in full. So this lane
carries what the agent's own planner reads, labelled, and the host decides how much authority
to give each fact under its own patterns.

Since the foreign lane admits admitted declared facts, the one thing this lane carries that the
block does not is content from an attacker-reachable channel an operator has released.

SilenceReason.description:
Why the answer has nothing to say about something, typed by MECHANISM rather than by meaning.

The question-shaped read solved "why is there no citation for this claim" with a typed
vocabulary. Nothing solved "why is there no claim for this question", and an empty answer is
read by a host model as "there is nothing", which is a different sentence from "your question
selected nothing" and from "we could not look".

Every member is decided from a claim the read holds, and none of them is a judgement about what
your question meant. That is what keeps the vocabulary honest: a reason that needed to
understand the question would need a model call, and this surface makes none.

`term_did_not_participate` is the one to read first. Names in a question are matched against the
entities this agent has recorded, exactly; everything else in the question selects nothing. So a
question asking for "a proven commercial win reusable as precedent" against an account selects on
the ACCOUNT and on nothing else, and this reason names the words that did no work. Without it, a
caller cannot tell an answer to their question from every claim we hold about a name it mentioned.

SupersessionReason.description:
Why an open version was closed, distinguishing update from revision.

WORLD_CHANGE: the world moved on (Katsuno-Mendelzon update); prior sources were
right, no reliability penalty. CORRECTION: a genuine conflict (revision); the
prior version's reliability interval widens. RETRACTION: withdrawn with no
replacement. REFINEMENT: narrowed to a more qualified claim.

The last three are all blameless closures the system performed on its own behalf, kept
distinct from WORLD_CHANGE so a synthesised chain is never later read as observed history.
ATTRIBUTE_MERGE: an offline merge put two keys in one class and their chains folded together.
ENTITY_MERGE: the same, one level up, where two surface forms were found to name one thing and
every slot of the two entities folded rather than one class of keys. Kept as its own member

post.description:
Reads the documents linked to the accounts your question names, and the documents its wording reaches, latest first, then writes an answer from what each one says.

Read `answer`; it can be null with a typed reason.

The default `detail=answer` level returns the answer, its `references`, the documents they name, `completeness` and `silence`; `completeness` is returned at every level. `detail=findings` adds `lead`, `findings`, `sections`, `results`, `appended_finding_ids`, `background_finding_ids`, `interpretation`, `subject`, `selection`, `multi_valued_slots`, `boundary`, `change`, `obligations`; `detail=claims` adds `claims`; `detail=everything` adds `read_documents`, `sources`, `stage_events`. Each level is the one before it plus its additions. A section at or below the level asked for is null when the step that produces it did not run for this answer, and an empty list when it ran and found nothing.

`budget_chars` lowers or raises how much document text is read, up to a ceiling. Past the budget the latest meetings are read first and the rest are chosen for relevance, labelled `earlier_history` so they are never stated as the current position.

Obligations are read at the time of the call rather than at `as_of`, which `obligations.is_as_of_pinned` states. Needs `claims:read` AND `agents:read`.

Synchronous, bounded only against a hang. The whole answer is stored as given for 30 days regardless of the `detail` asked for, so `GET /agents/{agent_id}/answers/{answer_id}` serves it again, word for word, at any level up to the one it names in `more`. A reused Idempotency-Key returns that same stored answer rather than composing again; a withheld answer is never billed and never holds the key, so a retry with it composes fresh. It earns no attribution.

delete.description: Erase this agent's entities and their claims, aliases, dossiers and split proposals, writing one receipt per entity, and drop the agent's attribute vocabulary once the last entity is gone. Each entity goes through the same erasure as the single-entity route, so the reinforcement its claims granted is withdrawn before the delete and no rule keeps standing on erased evidence. **One request erases a bounded batch**: the erasure is serial, so an unbounded pass over a large corpus would outrun the request. `remaining_entities` says how many are left, and a non-zero count means call again. Repeating is safe either way, because each entity's erasure is idempotent, so a retry after a timeout resumes rather than starting over. Answers 503 when some entities in a batch were erased and others could not be; the receipts already written stand. Like the single erasure this is a claim-layer erasure, not a full Article 17 erasure: learnings, graph nodes, raw run traces and usage aggregates are not deleted, and each receipt names them. The reason and ticket reference are an optional body; a client or proxy that drops a DELETE body loses only that context, never the erasure.

post.description:
Every claim this agent holds that bears on a question, across entities, as data. Unlike the recall path a turn uses, which caps its claim lane for prompt-injection reasons that are correct there, this read is not capped: it returns two arms with two different guarantees. The deterministic arm enumerates every claim on every entity the question's names reached, with a true total and deep stable paging, and says `exhaustive` when it managed that and `partial` when it did not. The recall arm is an approximate search, bounded and labelled `best_effort`. They are never blended into one total, because the checkable statement 'this is everything we hold about this account' is the product and an approximate scan cannot make it.

Read `deterministic.guarantee` and `is_total_exact` before quoting any number. Both sides of an unresolved contradiction are always returned and each names the other. Superseded values are excluded unless asked for; values that have merely gone stale are returned, marked. Rows held for human review are counted and never returned. Every row says how it was reached and where it was read from, and a row with no source says why it has none rather than arriving bare.

A POST because the question is free text of arbitrary length and the position is a structured token; it reads and writes nothing, records no run, and earns no attribution.

Store one submission under the caller's own document key and queue it for ingest. Returns 202 with the new version when work was enqueued, and 200 with the existing version when identical bytes are already stored: a 202 on a duplicate would promise work that will not happen. Refuses 409 when the tenant has no document key binding, 413 above the configured size ceiling, and 404 for an unknown agent, in each case without enqueueing anything.

The metadata is what links the document to its account and dates it, and the claims read from the document carry both. Metadata sent with bytes identical to a stored version is not applied, because nothing is re-read.

post.description: Distill durable learnings from post-mortems, documents, diffs, or analysis without inventing tool steps. Supply ``agent_name`` (your agent's human-readable name, not the hosted UUID from `/agents/{agent_id}`). If no agent with that name exists yet, one is created automatically on first use within your tenant. Creating a new name requires `agents:write`. Submit at least 1 evidence item. A request body is capped at 8 MiB. Where your tenant's items are stored as documents, each item becomes a document of the agent (keyed on its first `record_context.identifiers` entry as `scheme:value`, else its `source_ref`, else a hash of its text), claims cite the passage they came from, a resend of identical text costs nothing, and there is no item count or corpus total. Otherwise the corpus is capped at 200 items and 240,000 non-whitespace characters in total, and a single item may be the whole corpus. A corpus that declares no contrast is accepted rather than refused: contrast is what the learning extractor compares against, so a corpus without it can still be full of facts, and a run that yields nothing for that reason comes back as `zero_reason: weak_contrast` on `GET /learning-runs/{run_id}/status`, where a count stays null until the job finishes, which is not the same as zero. `run_id` is a caller-created idempotency and tracing value, must begin with `distill:`, and does not reference `GET /runs/{run_id}`. A valid request may yield no learning. Pre-redact secrets from evidence.

post.description: Create a domain space programmatically, so a connector or a test harness can provision its own container rather than waiting on someone to click. Requires an API key with the `spaces:write` scope and all-spaces reach; a key confined to selected spaces cannot create new ones. delete.description: Unregister a domain space, so the external container it mirrored resolves to nothing and its identifier is free for another space to take.
